- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) and prices are rising, model often underestimates the spike; increase forecast to match momentum.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high) — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust downward 1–2% if recent price is above 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate late-period price action (last 7–10 days) — add 0.5–1.5% buffer if sentiment is bullish or volatile.
- If sentiment is negative and model forecasts are rising, reverse the trend direction — model often misreads sentiment as bullish when it’s bearish.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is clearly negative (e.g., -0.30+); model tends to overcorrect and overshoot downward.
